title: 凉州词
author: Wang Zhihuan

translation: The Yellow River rises far into the white clouds
A single lonely town among ten-thousand-foot mountains
Why should the Qiang flute grieve over willows
When spring wind never crosses the Jade Gate Pass

annotations.仞: an ancient unit of length, about 2.3 meters — 万仞 is pure exaggeration for 'towering'
annotations.羌笛: a flute of the Qiang people — its plaintive sound stood for frontier sorrow
annotations.怨杨柳: to grieve over willows — willows symbolize parting, since 柳 liǔ puns on 留 liú 'to stay'
annotations.玉门关: Jade Gate Pass — the last outpost of the empire in the northwest desert

appreciation: A frontier poem of immense scale: river, clouds, mountains, and one tiny walled town lost among them. The closing line is a masterstroke of restraint — 'the spring wind never crosses the Jade Gate' means warmth, news, and home never reach these soldiers. No one complains outright; the flute does it for them.
